commons:3078150.summary: The Virgin sits enthroned in a deep blue robe, holding the Christ Child, who sits upright on her lap in a golden-brown garment with his own halo. Two soldier saints, Theodore and George, stand guard on either side holding crosses, while behind the throne two angels turn their faces upward. Painted in hot wax, the icon contrasts the still, frontal saints with the lively, almost classical angels, and is one of the rare icons to survive from before Byzantine Iconoclasm.
facts: Saint Catherine's Monastery is the only place where a substantial group of pre-iconoclastic encaustic icons survives, some dating as early as the 6th century.
No panel icons earlier than the few 6th-century examples preserved at Sinai survive in their original state.
commons:3078150.notes: 'Encaustic Virgin' is only the Commons file name; title supplied from the Commons description ('Virgin and Child with angels and Sts. George and Theodore'). Which saint stands on which side was not confirmed from a reliable source. Place of production is not documented.
